exposure: Mode of delivery (cesarean delivery, vaginal delivery)
cohort: The study included 1,983 nonsyndromic, liveborn neonates with spina bifida born in Texas between 1999 and 2014.
finding: After adjusting for potential confounders, there was no statistically significant difference in mortality risk prior to 29 days or 365 days between infants with spina bifida delivered by cesarean versus vaginally.
mod_finding: Cesarean delivery was not significantly associated with a reduced risk of death prior to 29 days or 365 days among infants with spina bifida.
